questions.stem: All cats are animals. Whiskers is a cat. What is Whiskers?
questions.explanation: If all cats are animals, Whiskers is one too. It follows straight from the first line.

questions.stem: There were 5 apples on the table. You took 2. How many apples do you have?
questions.explanation: The question is how many you have, not how many are left. You took 2, so you have 2.

questions.stem: Anna is taller than Boris, and Boris is taller than Victor. Who is the shortest?
questions.explanation: Line them up: Anna, Boris, Victor. Victor is below Boris, who is below Anna.

questions.stem: A bag holds 3 red balls and 2 blue. How many must you draw blind to be sure of a red?
questions.explanation: Worst case both blue ones come out first. The third ball is certainly red.

questions.stem: When it rains, the ground is wet. The ground is wet. Is it definitely raining?
questions.explanation: Someone could have watered the garden. Wet ground does not prove rain.

questions.stem: All roses are flowers. Some flowers wilt fast. Does that mean all roses wilt fast?
questions.explanation: "Some" is not "all". The fast-wilting flowers could be entirely different ones.

questions.stem: Which is heavier: a kilo of cotton wool or a kilo of iron?
questions.explanation: A kilo is a kilo. Iron only seems heavier because it takes up far less room.

questions.stem: Every gnome has a beard. Petya has no beard. Could Petya be a gnome?
questions.explanation: If Petya were a gnome he would have a beard. He has none, so he is not one.

questions.stem: Continue the sequence: 2, 4, 8, 16, …
questions.explanation: Each number doubles the last one rather than adding two. After 16 comes 32.

questions.stem: Continue the sequence: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, …
questions.explanation: Each number is the sum of the two before it: 2 + 3 = 5, so next is 3 + 5 = 8.

questions.stem: In a race you overtake the runner in second place. What position are you in now?
questions.explanation: You took the place of the one you passed. The leader is still ahead of you.

questions.stem: It is false that all birds fly. What follows from that?
questions.explanation: Denying "all" gives "at least one does not", not "none of them do".

questions.stem: What would disprove the claim "all swans are white"?
questions.explanation: A universal claim falls to a single exception. More white swans never settle it.

questions.stem: How many times can you subtract 5 from the number 25?
questions.explanation: After the first subtraction it is no longer 25 but 20. From 25 you can only do it once.

questions.stem: If A implies B, and B turns out false, what can be said about A?
questions.explanation: Were A true, B would be true as well. B is false, so A must be false too.

questions.stem: The claim: "no pupil was late". What would disprove it?
questions.explanation: A single case is enough to make "no pupil" stop being true.

questions.stem: In summer both ice cream sales and drownings rise. Is ice cream dangerous?
questions.explanation: Both rise because of the heat. Moving together does not make one the cause of the other.

questions.stem: A survey on whether the internet is useful polled only internet users. What is wrong?
questions.explanation: Nobody asked the people who do not use it. The answer was decided by who was asked.

questions.stem: A remedy helped 9 of 10 volunteers. What is missing before we believe it?
questions.explanation: Without a comparison we cannot tell whether the remedy helped or people simply recovered.

questions.stem: "Whoever is not with us is against us." What is wrong with this reasoning?
questions.explanation: One can simply be indifferent or unaware. The choice of two was imposed, not proved.
